text:
leo: Quick quarterly pattern check-in (Jan	60Mar). Pulled every P1/P2 postmortem and clustered by contributing factor. Sharing highlights + ask: owners for the remediation themes so we can track recurrence into Q2.

anya: Thanks Leo. What's the high-level breakdown?

leo: Short version: three recurring themes cover ~72% of repeat pages: 1) model-serving deploy regressions (config drift + canary gaps), 2) autoscaling mispredictions (under-provision at peak), 3) stateful cache evictions causing increased latencies. Others are smaller: infra network flaps, RBAC/permission errors, vendor throttles.

ram: Can you share the counts and recurrence window you used?

leo: Used 90-day window, recurrence = same service impacted >2 incidents. Raw counts: 
```
model-deploy-regressions: 18
autoscale-mispredictions: 11
cache-evictions/state loss: 9
network-flaps: 4
permission-errors: 3
third-party-rate: 2
other: 6
TOTAL reviewed: 53
```

kevin: Not surprising. For deploy regressions, are we mostly seeing config drift between envs or test coverage gaps?

leo: Both. 10 were canary pass criteria too permissive; 5 were config drift (different defaults in dedicated vs hosted); 3 were incomplete compatibility checks for new model artifacts.

emily: Autoscaler stuff	6 how many are due to policy tuning vs bad telemetry?

leo: Policy tuning (7) where scale-down aggressiveness was high; telemetry gaps (4) where the workload shape wasn't visible to the controller (short bursts).

anya: Cache evictions	6 is this the same KV namespace we saw last month?

leo: Yes, mostly the session-cache namespace. Root causes: increased ingestion (retention config change) and a leaking balloon from a background job.

ops-bot: Automated note: related postmortems referenced: PM-3412, PM-3420, PM-3437, PM-3451. Link PRs with #incident-q1 to enable tracking.

leo: Proposed thematic remediations (brief):
A) Harden canary criteria + add smoke traffic + environment parity checks.
B) Autoscaler: add burst-aware policy + conservative min-instances for critical routes + replay-driven simulator.
C) Cache: set strict memory quotas per namespace, eviction-rate alert, and nightly compaction for known leaks.
D) Add 'deployment health' dashboard that correlates canary metrics with error budgets.

anya: I can take A) with help from Platform QA. Will sketch doc and schedule a working session.

ram: I can lead B). Plan: prototype simulator (ram + kevin) and propose conservative min-instance defaults for SLO-critical routes.

kevin: Ack. Ram, I'll start with a replay harness that uses recent request traces. Also want a quick experiment with increasing min-instance to see cost impact.

emily: I'll own C). I'll also add eviction-rate as a Slack alert first (no page) and escalate to pager if unresolved 20m.

leo: Thanks. Can we set owners + realistic due dates for tracking in the follow-up dashboard? Aim for Q2 sprint milestones. Draft below; tweak as needed.

Assigned items (owner	6 due):
1) Canary + env-parity checklist + smoke traffic job	6 owner: anya	6 due: 2026-05-10
2) Autoscaler simulator + burst-aware policy proposal	6 owner: ram	6 due: 2026-05-17
3) Min-instance defaults for critical routes (ops change)	6 owner: kevin	6 due: 2026-05-12
4) Cache namespace quotas + eviction alerts + compaction job	6 owner: emily	6 due: 2026-05-05
5) Deployment health dashboard (correlate canary pass/fail with error budget)	6 owner: leo	6 due: 2026-05-24
6) Quarterly recurrence report: measure 'recurrence rate' and median time-to-remediation per theme	6 owner: ops-bot (automated)	6 due: 2026-05-31

kevin: Small ask	6 can we include cost delta estimates for autoscaler min-instance changes? I'll add a short section in the simulator PR.

ram: Sounds good. Also propose a short retro in the SRE-All hands for May week 2 to walk through the themes and prioritization.

anya: ACK on A), will post initial checklist by 2026-04-22 and invite reviewers.

emily: ACK on C), will create the dashboard and alert and post links here by 2026-05-03.

leo: One operational note: set follow-up tickets to P2 and tag with #incident-q1. If a remediation touches multiple services, list them explicitly so the follow-up tracker can map recurrence.

ops-bot: Reminder: add single-line ticket status updates when you start work. The follow-up tracker aggregates weekly; missing updates will show as 'stalled'.

kevin: Will do. Also, can we track 'post-remediation recurrence' at 30/60/90d windows? That would help validate fixes.

leo: Good idea. Adding 30/60/90 recurrence checks to the quarterly report.

ram: One more thought	6 for model-deploy regressions, maybe add an artifact-contract test to assert model schema + quantization format before deploy.

anya: I'll include artifact-contract checks in the canary checklist.

leo: Great. I'll update the consolidation spreadsheet with owners and due dates and ping this thread when it's live. If owners need to shift deadlines, reply here. Meeting: I'll book a 20min working session next Tue to kick off A+B.

kevin: Thanks Leo	6 this framing helps.

emily: :thumbsup:
